citation.title: Chapter 8: Plasma operation and control
citation.authors: ITER Physics Expert Group on Disruptions, Plasma Control, and MHD; ITER Physics Expert Group on Energetic Particles, Heating and Current Drive; ITER Physics Expert Group on Diagnostics; ITER Physics Basis Editors

topic: ITER physics-basis review of wall conditioning, magnetic and kinetic control, scenario design, and advanced-tokamak profile control.
own_question: How present tokamak control experience extrapolates to ITER control requirements.
actual_method_and_evidence: Review that compiles control experience from multiple devices, including a kinetic-control experience table (Table 3), and reports ITER control simulations (TSC, PRETOR). It contains no CES, BES, or ECEI nowcasting, no ion-temperature estimation, and no data-driven estimators.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: ITER-era control planning anticipated that accurate real-time measurement of q/j and electron and ion pressure profiles would be critical for advanced-scenario control.
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' stated requirement, not a demonstrated capability. It concerns pressure profiles generally and does not address impurity CES Ti.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The source has no CES report timing, latency, or 10 ms computation data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim the source shows that Ti nowcasting is needed or feasible.
Do not claim it addresses CES latency, BES, or ECEI.
Do not treat the listed ITER requirements as achieved performance.
Do not generalize this source to all prior work.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most, this could serve as a general motivation citation for real-time profile measurement in control. It provides no evidence on our specific problem, so including it is optional.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
